title: Scheduled echopoint suite reported a false failure: one TCP reset on a login failed the whole flow because the runner never retries a node
summary: In the 17:08Z scheduled suite run, `echopoint: health monitors` failed in 353 ms on its first node: the `POST https://apidev.tryanchor.dev/v1/auth/login` connection from the laptop was reset by the peer (Cloudflare edge address). Anchor was healthy: 36 other flows logged in to the same host within the same minute and passed. The runner has a retry middleware but no production code wires it, so a single transport error fails the node and the flow. `run_suites.sh` only reran lease-expired flows, so the failure was printed like a product failure and needed manual triage. Two reruns passed. `run_suites.sh` now reruns once any flow that failed on a transport error before a response from a dev API, and the flow-suite-testing skill names this diagnosis class.

impact.text: One false red flow in the echopoint suite (36/37). Dev APIs only, no customer impact, nothing created before the failure so nothing leaked.

trigger: The TCP connection carrying the `login` POST to `apidev.tryanchor.dev` (172.64.80.1:443) was reset by the peer at 17:11:13Z.
detection: `run_suites.sh` printed `FAILED echopoint ce39b646…: Could not connect to apidev.tryanchor.dev … connection reset by peer` at the end of the run, 91 s after the failure. Detection was good enough: the script reads each failed flow's error. Only the classification was missing.
resolution: The flow was rerun twice by hand at 17:12:55Z and 17:12:58Z, both green. `run_suites.sh` now does the rerun itself and prints `TRANSPORT-RERUN` so the cause stays visible.

events.label: Scheduled routine run starts on AC power
events.detail: `pmset -g batt`: AC Power, 100%. No sleep/wake in the run window.

events.label: echopoint tag starts (37 flows, embedded CLI runner)
events.detail: First execution `01a15f71-3f5a…` (UUIDv7 time). Patched CLI from `feat/workspace-auth` because of the open SEV2 on released CLIs.

events.label: `login` POST reset by peer; flow fails
events.detail: Execution `01a15f72-1151-728d-82f7-06feaf5776a8`, started 17:11:13.489Z, failed 17:11:13.842Z: `read tcp 192.168.2.50:52576->172.64.80.1:443: read: connection reset by peer`. Cleanup nodes skipped: no upstream output existed.

events.label: run_suites.sh prints FAILED with the transport error
events.detail: echopoint 36/37. The rerun rule only matched `runner lease expired before completion`.

events.label: run_suites.sh reruns transport failures once; skill lesson

whys.problem: The scheduled echopoint suite reported `echopoint: health monitors` red with no product defect

because.text: Its first node `login` failed `CONNECTION_FAILED`: the TCP connection to apidev.tryanchor.dev was reset by the peer
because.evidence: runs/2026-10-21T17/echopoint.log line 40: `error_code: CONNECTION_FAILED … read: connection reset by peer`

because.text: The reset came from the path between the laptop and Cloudflare's edge, not from Anchor: 36 flows logged in to the same host that minute
because.evidence: Same run: 36/37 echopoint and 24/24 anchor green; apidev.tryanchor.dev /health HEALTHY 23dc3796 at 17:08Z

because.text: Which hop sent the reset (home router, ISP, Cloudflare edge closing a pooled keep-alive connection) is not known
The dogfood suites run from a laptop on a residential network, not from a host with a stable, observed network path
because.evidence: Same host decision as the 2026-10-17 host-sleep postmortem (action A3 there, still open)

because.text: One transport error failed the whole flow: the runner never retries a node, and flows have no per-node retry option
because.evidence: echopoint-runner v0.94.0 and main: `engine.Retry` / `runner.Retry` are called only from tests and docs (`git grep 'Retry('`)

because.text: Go's http.Transport replays a request on a dead connection only when it is idempotent; the login is a POST
because.evidence: net/http Transport docs: retries only idempotent requests (or ones with an Idempotency-Key header) on reused connections

because.text: No runner policy says when a transport failure before any response is safe to replay (method, http_calls counting, limits)
Why so bad: the run printed the failure like a product failure and needed manual triage
because.evidence: run_suites.sh printed `FAILED echopoint ce39b646…`, not a rerun

because.text: run_suites.sh reran only lease-expired flows; transport errors fell through to FAILED
because.evidence: run_suites.sh before 2026-10-21: one branch on `runner lease expired before completion`

because.text: The suite's host-cause rules listed one class (lease expiry) instead of every failure that happens before the product answers

contributing: The suites currently run on a CLI built from an unmerged branch (open SEV2 on released CLIs), so the run already carried manual steps.
The node error carries a code (`CONNECTION_FAILED`) in the runner log but the execution list only returns the message, so the script matches message prefixes.

well: run_suites.sh reads each failed flow's error, so the transport cause was visible in the run output.
The runner's error classifier named the class (`CONNECTION_FAILED`) and kept the raw cause.
wrong: The host-cause rule from 2026-10-17 covered one symptom, not the class.
A runner retry middleware has existed for months without a production caller or a decision on it.
lucky: The reset hit the first node. On a create node (for example `create-org`) after the server had written, the `always` cleanup that reads its output would be skipped (`Source node not executed yet`) and a throwaway org could leak.
The suite is dev-only; the same reset on a Cloud monitor would fail a customer's run with no replay.

actions.what: Decide and implement a runner policy for transport failures before any response: e.g. replay once for idempotent methods or nodes marked retryable, count the replay in `http_calls`
`run_suites.sh` reruns once a flow that failed on a transport error (connect/reset, refused, TLS, DNS) before a response from a dev API and prints `TRANSPORT-RERUN`; a second failure stays FAILED
flow-suite-testing skill: a transport failure before a response is a host or network cause; rerun once, a repeat is an outage
Decide the suite host (always-on host or Cloud launches); same decision as the 2026-10-17 host-sleep postmortem A3
Sweep throwaway Anchor orgs that outlive their flow run (dev nanostack product), so a skipped cleanup cannot accumulate

messaging.internal: Suite 17:08Z: `echopoint: health monitors` red on a TCP reset to apidev.tryanchor.dev (laptop network), green on rerun x2. No product defect. run_suites.sh now reruns transport failures once.
